category_title: Highly gifted female prioritizing social survival and employment over academic performance
minimal_context: Mariah and the tutor are discussing her options beyond dropping out during the week caps and gowns are distributed.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Mariah, they are handing out caps and gowns and tickets this week. Since you are not graduating, we need to discuss your options beyond dropping out.

STUDENT: I know I need to do better. I want to be the person that I know is inside of me so I can be proud of her. But I don't want to talk about this right now.

TUTOR: What are your thoughts on the alternative programs?

STUDENT: I'm not looking at them. Honestly, I'm just denying the fact that any of this is happening right now.

TUTOR: You need to make a decision about what to do next.

STUDENT: I don't want to hear your ideas about it. I already work full-time, so I'll just figure it out and be okay.

options.A: Build a meaningful, affective relationship focused on the growth and development of the whole student, acting as a mentor and counselor in a non-threatening and sincere way.
options.B: Implement a minimal yet demanding curriculum centered on a single 15-page research paper to simulate real-world postsecondary expectations for the student.
options.C: Teach the student how to enter information into a daily tracking form, having her check the appropriate box at the end of each session and turn it in for verification.
options.D: Set up a token system to target the student's academic performance, listing five specific goals for each session and checking off boxes as the student completes target behaviors.
